ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the middle of the figure is an azo structure N=N, and the nitrogens at the two ends are each connected by a single bond to the adjacent substituted carbon; beside these carbons, NC/CN in the direction of cyano groups are labeled, and they bear methyl line-segment substituents. In the figure, curved arrows go from near the C–N single bonds on both sides and from the N=N bond region toward the nitrogen-nitrogen bonding region, indicating electron redistribution. Reasoning: After pushing arrows, the C–N single bonds on both sides that connect to the azo nitrogens are broken, and the central N=N obtains additional bond order to form nitrogen gas N#N. The broken carbon part remains as an independent cyano-substituted carbon fragment and is transcribed as specified as C[C](C#N). Because the products are two disconnected species, they are connected with a dot in SMILES, therefore giving N#N.C[C](C#N).

method.method_draft: First identify the bonds and arrows in the image. Apply the arrows: remove the C–N single bonds to the azo nitrogens, convert the central N=N into N#N, and leave the carbon substituent as a separate cyano-substituted carbon fragment. Translate the disconnected nitrogen molecule as N#N and the carbon fragment as C[C](C#N), then join disconnected species with a dot to obtain N#N.C[C](C#N).
